about.title: About
about.disclaimer:
This app is for entertainment purposes only. Readings are random and do not constitute professional advice or an in-person consultation. For important decisions, seek advice from a qualified professional.

Your path is shaped by your choices. The cards offer perspectives, but you remain the author of your life. Trust your intuition, move step by step, and take care of yourself.

major_00.signification reversed: You may be resisting a necessary ending, clinging to what no longer serves you. This can lead to stagnation, emotional exhaustion, and missed opportunities for growth. Accepting change, even when painful, allows for healing and renewal. Take time to grieve, but do not let fear of the unknown prevent you from moving forward. Sometimes, holding on is more damaging than letting go.
major_00.signification upright: Death marks a profound transformation—a closing of one chapter and the beginning of another. Though endings can be difficult, they clear space for new experiences, wisdom, and growth. Embrace the process of release, honor what has passed, and trust that renewal follows. This card encourages you to let go of old patterns, relationships, or beliefs that have run their course. In doing so, you make room for vitality, hope, and new beginnings.
major_00.upright: transformation, end of a cycle, rebirth
major_00.name: Death

major_01.reversed: denial of growth, harsh judgment, guilt
major_01.signification reversed: You may be struggling with guilt, regret, or an inability to forgive yourself or others. Harsh self-judgment or denial of personal growth can keep you stuck in the past. This card asks you to reflect honestly, release blame, and seek compassion. True renewal comes from accepting responsibility and making amends, not from punishment or avoidance. Allow yourself to move forward with mercy and self-acceptance.
major_01.signification upright: Judgement heralds a time of awakening, self-evaluation, and transformation. You are called to review your life, acknowledge lessons learned, and embrace a higher purpose. This card encourages forgiveness—of yourself and others—and the courage to answer your true calling. It is a moment to let go of past mistakes, accept your growth, and step into a new phase with clarity and conviction. Renewal and redemption are possible now.
major_01.name: Judgement

major_02.signification reversed: Justice reversed warns of unfairness, dishonesty, or unresolved conflicts. You may be facing bias, corruption, or a situation where the truth is obscured. Be cautious of making hasty decisions or seeking revenge. Instead, strive for accountability and repair. If you feel wronged, seek resolution through honest dialogue and fair process. This card also asks you to examine your own actions and motives—are you acting with integrity?
major_02.signification upright: Justice represents truth, fairness, and the need for balanced decisions. It calls you to act with integrity, weigh all sides carefully, and accept responsibility for your choices. Legal matters, contracts, or ethical dilemmas may be at play, and clarity is essential. This card encourages transparency, honesty, and the pursuit of what is right—not just what is easy. When you honor fairness, you set a precedent for future harmony and trust.
major_02.name: Justice

major_03.image_reversed: tarot_img/MajorArcanaCards/Le Roi de Coupe a l'envers.jpg
major_03.reversed: emotional manipulation, calculated coldness, hidden instability
major_03.signification reversed: The King of Cups reversed can indicate emotional manipulation, coldness, or hidden instability. You may be struggling to manage your feelings, or someone around you is using emotions to control or unsettle. Beware of passive-aggressive behavior, mood swings, or a lack of empathy. This card asks you to set healthy boundaries and seek emotional balance, rather than suppressing or weaponizing your feelings.
major_03.signification upright: The King of Cups upright represents emotional mastery, compassion, and wise leadership. You are able to navigate turbulent waters with calm and understanding, offering support to others without losing yourself. This card encourages you to lead with empathy, listen deeply, and mediate fairly. Your ability to balance heart and mind brings harmony to relationships and situations.
major_03.upright: emotional mastery, wise compassion, benevolent leadership
major_03.name: King of Cups

major_04.image_reversed: tarot_img/MajorArcanaCards/Le Roi De Deniers a l'envers.jpg
major_04.signification reversed: The King of Pentacles reversed warns of greed, corruption, or an unhealthy fixation on material success. You may be prioritizing wealth over values, or feeling trapped by financial concerns. This card asks you to examine your relationship with money and power—are you using resources to help others, or only to serve yourself? True prosperity is shared and ethical.
major_04.signification upright: The King of Pentacles upright signifies established prosperity, wise stewardship, and responsible leadership. You have built something durable and valuable, and now is the time to share your success. Invest patiently, protect those in your care, and model ethical behavior. Your grounded approach inspires trust and long-term growth.
major_04.upright: established prosperity, wise stewardship, material leadership
major_04.name: King of Pentacles

major_05.reversed: coldness, abuse of power, manipulative intellect
major_05.signification reversed: The King of Swords reversed can indicate coldness, abuse of power, or manipulative intellect. You may be using logic to dominate or distance yourself from others, or someone in your life is acting ruthlessly. This card asks you to temper intellect with compassion, and to use your authority to serve, not control. Beware of harsh judgments and inflexible thinking.
major_05.signification upright: The King of Swords upright represents clear reason, just authority, and objective decision-making. You are able to analyze situations with precision, speak truthfully, and act with integrity. Let ethics guide your strategy, and use your intellect to uplift and protect. Fairness and clarity are your strengths now.
major_05.name: King of Swords

major_06.image_reversed: tarot_img/MajorArcanaCards/Le Roi De Baton a l'envers.jpg
major_06.reversed: impulsive domination, hot-headed rule, ego-driven moves
major_06.signification reversed: The King of Wands reversed warns of impulsive domination, ego-driven decisions, or hot-headed leadership. You may be acting out of pride, seeking control, or ignoring the needs of others. This card asks you to listen, share power, and channel your energy into partnership rather than intimidation. True influence is earned through respect and collaboration.
major_06.signification upright: The King of Wands upright embodies charismatic leadership, visionary action, and creative direction. You inspire others with your passion and boldness, rallying allies and setting ambitious goals. Courage and clarity ignite progress—lead with purpose, remove obstacles, and encourage innovation. Your fire brings light to those around you.
major_06.upright: charismatic leadership, visionary action, creative direction
major_06.name: King of Wands

major_07.image_reversed: tarot_img/MajorArcanaCards/Le Cavalier De Coupe a l'envers.jpg
major_07.reversed: romantic illusions, empty promises, emotional games
major_07.signification reversed: The Knight of Cups reversed can signal romantic illusions, empty promises, or emotional games. You may be swept up in fantasy, or someone is offering affection without sincerity. This card asks you to look beneath the surface—test for substance, and choose honesty over performance. Beware of being led astray by charm or wishful thinking.
major_07.signification upright: The Knight of Cups upright represents romance, invitation, and creative proposal. You are ready to extend heartfelt offers—whether in art, love, or reconciliation. Let sincerity guide your actions, and express your feelings openly. This card encourages you to pursue beauty, connection, and emotional fulfillment with grace and authenticity.
major_07.name: Knight of Cups

major_08.image_reversed: tarot_img/MajorArcanaCards/Le Cavalier de Deniers a l'envers.jpg
major_08.signification reversed: The Knight of Pentacles reversed can indicate stagnation, laziness, or a lack of ambition. You may be feeling stuck in a rut, avoiding responsibilities, or neglecting important tasks. This card asks you to break free from inertia by setting small, achievable goals and taking consistent action. Progress comes from discipline and perseverance, not from waiting for motivation.
major_08.signification upright: The Knight of Pentacles upright represents diligence, method, and perseverance. You are reliable, hardworking, and committed to steady progress. This card encourages you to refine your process, track your achievements, and build security through consistent effort. Success is earned over time—trust in your ability to see things through.
major_08.name: Knight of Pentacles

major_09.signification reversed: The Knight of Swords reversed warns of aggression, impulsiveness, or reckless action. You may be charging ahead without considering consequences, or letting anger drive your decisions. This card asks you to slow down, check your motives, and correct your aim before taking action. True courage is guided by wisdom, not by force.
major_09.signification upright: The Knight of Swords upright signifies bold action, resolve, and rapid change. You are ready to advance with courage and clarity, cutting through obstacles with determination. This card encourages you to act decisively, communicate directly, and pursue your goals with focus. Speed and purpose combine for powerful results.
major_09.name: Knight of Swords

major_10.image_reversed: tarot_img/MajorArcanaCards/Le Cavalier de Baton a l'envers.jpg
major_10.signification reversed: The Knight of Wands reversed can indicate haste, scattered effort, or fleeing from challenges. You may be rushing without a plan, or abandoning projects before completion. This card asks you to ground your energy, focus your intentions, and channel your speed into purposeful action. Progress is made by balancing enthusiasm with discipline.
major_10.signification upright: The Knight of Wands upright represents adventure, momentum, and swift initiative. You are ready to start fast, learn quickly, and embrace daring moves. This card encourages you to pilot new ideas, accept feedback, and iterate in motion. Your energy and passion drive you forward—use them wisely to achieve your aims.
major_10.name: Knight of Wands

major_11.image_reversed: tarot_img/MajorArcanaCards/Le Valet De Coupe a l'envers.jpg
major_11.signification reversed: The Page of Cups reversed can signal emotional immaturity, hurt feelings, or creative blockage. You may be struggling to express yourself, or feeling vulnerable and misunderstood. This card asks you to soothe your wounds gently, create in small, safe ways, and seek support when needed. Healing comes from self-acceptance and honest communication.
major_11.signification upright: The Page of Cups upright represents emotional messages, artistic inspiration, and tender openings. You are invited to express your feelings, explore your creativity, and approach life with curiosity and openness. This card encourages gentle communication, new beginnings in relationships, and the birth of creative ideas.
major_11.upright: emotional message, artistic spark, tender opening
major_11.name: Page of Cups

major_12.image_reversed: tarot_img/MajorArcanaCards/Le Valet De Deniers a l'envers.jpg
major_12.signification reversed: The Page of Pentacles reversed warns of superficial study, neglect, or a shortcut mindset. You may be avoiding the hard work needed for mastery, or failing to invest in your growth. This card asks you to trade quick fixes for lasting habits, and to commit to learning through repeated care and effort. True progress is built on solid foundations.
major_12.signification upright: The Page of Pentacles upright signifies applied study, new material opportunities, and diligence. You are ready to lay foundations, learn by doing, and improve your skills. This card encourages you to ship small projects, invest in tangible growth, and build security through practical effort. Curiosity and persistence will serve you well.
major_12.upright: applied study, new material chance, diligence
major_12.name: Page of Pentacles

major_13.signification reversed: The Page of Swords reversed can indicate indiscretion, rumors, or manipulation of information. You may be tempted to gossip, spread misinformation, or act impulsively with words. This card asks you to pause, verify facts, and consider the impact of your communication. Sometimes, wisdom is found in silence and careful listening.
major_13.signification upright: The Page of Swords upright represents keen curiosity, important news, and vigilance. You are encouraged to observe sharply, ask insightful questions, and communicate responsibly. This card brings new ideas, messages, or opportunities for learning. Stay alert, be honest, and use your intellect to seek truth.
major_13.name: Page of Swords

major_14.image_reversed: tarot_img/MajorArcanaCards/Le Valet de Baton a l'envers.jpg
major_14.signification reversed: The Page of Wands reversed warns of empty promises, shallow enthusiasm, or impatience. You may be starting projects without finishing them, or losing interest quickly. This card asks you to stay committed past the first hurdle, deepen your engagement, and develop your ideas with patience and persistence. True creativity requires dedication.
major_14.signification upright: The Page of Wands upright represents creative messages, new ideas, and youthful excitement. You are invited to announce, test, and practice your inspirations. Curiosity is your teacher now—embrace new opportunities, experiment boldly, and let your enthusiasm guide you. Growth comes from exploration and play.
major_14.upright: creative message, new idea, youthful excitement
major_14.name: Page of Wands

major_15.image_reversed: tarot_img/MajorArcanaCards/La Reine De Coupe a l'envers.jpg
major_15.signification reversed: The Queen of Cups reversed can signal over-emotionality, dependency, or self-erasing sacrifice. You may be giving too much, losing yourself in the needs of others, or struggling to set boundaries. This card asks you to refill your own cup, nurture yourself, and remember that compassion needs healthy limits to last. Emotional balance is key to true empathy.
major_15.signification upright: The Queen of Cups upright represents deep intuition, true empathy, and unconditional love. You offer sanctuary and skilled listening, healing others with your presence and understanding. This card encourages you to trust your feelings, care for yourself and those around you, and set gentle boundaries. Empathy with wisdom brings lasting connection.
major_15.upright: deep intuition, true empathy, unconditional love
major_15.name: Queen of Cups

major_16.image_reversed: tarot_img/MajorArcanaCards/La Reine De Deniers a l'envers.jpg
major_16.signification reversed: The Queen of Pentacles reversed warns of overprotective materialism, neglect of home, or wastefulness. You may be focusing too much on possessions, or letting practical matters slide. This card asks you to re-order your priorities, reduce clutter, and revive simple, steady care for yourself and your environment. True abundance is nurtured, not hoarded.
major_16.signification upright: The Queen of Pentacles upright signifies nurturing abundance, practical care, and shared prosperity. You create safety, warmth, and flourishing systems for yourself and others. This card encourages practical kindness, generosity, and the cultivation of well-being. Prosperity grows when shared and tended with love.
major_16.upright: nurturing abundance, practical care, shared prosperity
major_16.name: Queen of Pentacles

major_17.signification reversed: The Queen of Swords reversed can indicate bitterness, resentment, or cutting criticism. You may be using words as weapons, or struggling to forgive past hurts. This card asks you to heal your wounds before speaking, and to temper honesty with kindness. True clarity is sharpened by compassion, not by harshness.
major_17.signification upright: The Queen of Swords upright represents independence, lucidity, candid truth, and pragmatic insight. You are able to name realities cleanly, set respectful boundaries, and help others grow through honest feedback. This card encourages you to balance intellect with empathy, and to use your wisdom to guide and protect. Clarity with kindness is your strength.
major_17.upright: independence, lucidity, candid truth, pragmatic insight
major_17.name: Queen of Swords

major_18.image_reversed: tarot_img/MajorArcanaCards/La Reine de Baton a l'envers.jpg
major_18.signification reversed: The Queen of Wands reversed can indicate jealousy, possessiveness, or creative blockage. You may be comparing yourself to others, feeling insecure, or struggling to express your creativity. This card asks you to reclaim play, restore healthy boundaries, and create from self-trust rather than competition. True inspiration comes from within.
major_18.signification upright: The Queen of Wands upright represents radiant creativity, warm generosity, and inspiring presence. Your warmth sparks rooms and projects, championing others and playing big. This card encourages you to keep joy central to your creative process, share your gifts freely, and lead with confidence. Your energy uplifts and motivates those around you.
major_18.upright: radiant creativity, warm generosity, inspiring presence
major_18.name: Queen of Wands

major_19.reversed: weakness, loss of control, aggression, avoidance
major_19.signification reversed: Strength reversed can signal weakness, loss of control, aggression, or avoidance. You may be struggling to manage your impulses, feeling overwhelmed, or avoiding challenges. This card asks you to slow your breath, set simple boundaries, and rebuild strength from within through small, brave acts. True power is gentle and self-regulated.
major_19.signification upright: Strength upright represents inner strength, patience, compassion, and courage. You are able to regulate the storm, meeting force with presence rather than panic. This card encourages you to tame what is wild within and around you, using courage and kindness to earn trust. In love and work, gentle power is the key to lasting success.
major_19.name: Strength

major_20.signification reversed: Temperance reversed warns of imbalance, excess, haste, or chaotic mixing. You may be overdoing or neglecting something important, leading to disharmony. This card asks you to remove one excess, add one stabilizer, and let time do its part. Healing and integration require patience and careful calibration.
major_20.signification upright: Temperance upright represents balance, healing, patience, and harmonious blending. You are able to mix opposites with care, allowing healing to ripen gradually. This card encourages you to calibrate your inputs, pace, and boundaries, integrating rather than oscillating. True harmony is achieved through moderation and thoughtful adjustment.
major_20.name: Temperance

major_21.reversed: loss of control, scattered energy, misdirection
major_21.signification reversed: The Chariot reversed can indicate loss of control, scattered energy, or misdirection. You may be struggling to focus, forcing outcomes, or resisting necessary adjustments. This card asks you to loosen your grip, refine your goals, and realign your efforts with meaning. Success comes from disciplined momentum, not frantic speed.
major_21.signification upright: The Chariot upright represents mastery of opposing forces, determination, and victory. You are able to define your finish line, set constraints, and keep promises to yourself. This card encourages you to pull together divergent energies, focus on repeatable wins, and move forward with disciplined momentum. True victory is earned through clarity and perseverance.
major_21.upright: mastery of opposing forces, determination, victory
major_21.name: The Chariot

major_22.signification reversed: The Devil reversed signals liberation, awakening, or breaking chains. You are ready to free yourself from unhealthy attachments, addictions, or limiting beliefs. This card asks you to choose one clean break or boundary—freedom expands from there. Awareness and conscious choice dissolve the illusion of bondage.
major_22.signification upright: The Devil upright represents attachments, illusions, materialism, and temptation. You may be facing habits, debts, obsessions, or toxic bonds that cloud your judgment. This card encourages you to name the chains, bring awareness to your patterns, and reclaim your power. Desire is not evil, but unconscious compulsion can be. Seek clarity and self-mastery.
major_22.name: The Devil

major_23.reversed: tyranny, rigidity, abuse of power, control issues
major_23.signification reversed: The Emperor reversed can indicate tyranny, rigidity, or abuse of power. You may be struggling with control issues, micromanagement, or inflexible leadership. This card asks you to replace fear-based command with clear goals and autonomy. True strength is flexible, accountable, and fair—lead by empowering others, not by dominating them.
major_23.signification upright: The Emperor upright represents authority, structure, stability, and responsibility. You are called to build frameworks that serve people, set boundaries, and use strategy and foresight to turn chaos into order. Lead by example, make decisions transparent, and protect the vulnerable. Calm, fair order is a kindness to all.
major_23.name: The Emperor

major_24.signification reversed: The Empress reversed warns of creative block, smothering, or over-control. You may be holding on too tightly, over-giving to be needed, or struggling with dependence. This card asks you to step back, breathe, and reconnect to cycles of rest and ripening. Allow help, release perfectionism, and trust the natural process of growth.
major_24.signification upright: The Empress upright represents fertility, abundance, creativity, nourishment, and nature. Life blossoms when you create, nurture, and let things grow in their own rhythm. Pleasure, beauty, and care replenish your field. Invest in body, home, and art; receive as you give. Collaboration and generosity multiply results.
major_24.name: The Empress

major_25.signification reversed: The Fool reversed can indicate recklessness, naivety, carelessness, or hesitation. You may be acting impulsively, escaping discomfort, or fearing commitment. This card asks you to slow down, sense consequences, and set simple guardrails. Begin wisely, with presence and intention—curiosity is good, but awareness is essential.
major_25.signification upright: The Fool upright represents new beginnings, spontaneity, freedom, adventure, and potential. A clean slate invites trust, curiosity, and play. Take first steps before certainty appears, follow what feels alive, and travel light. In love, bring honesty and openness; in work, prototype and learn in motion. You don’t need every answer to begin—just a sincere yes.
major_25.upright: new beginnings, spontaneity, freedom, adventure, potential
major_25.name: The Fool

major_26.signification reversed: The Hanged Man reversed warns of stalled sacrifice, stubbornness, or resisting change. You may be hanging on without learning, or letting pride block flexibility. This card asks you to surrender a little, allow movement, and open to new perspectives. Growth comes from letting go, not from clinging.
major_26.signification upright: The Hanged Man upright represents sacrifice, new perspective, surrender, and patience. Suspend action to see differently, yield the old angle, and pivot into wisdom. Surrender is not defeat—it is a path to insight and elegant next moves.
major_26.name: The Hanged Man

major_27.signification reversed: The Hermit reversed can indicate isolation, rejecting advice, or stubbornness. You may be hiding from connection, blocking counsel, or letting loneliness harden your heart. This card asks you to re-enter connection gently, seek wisdom, and remain teachable. Solitude is valuable only when it leads to growth.
major_27.signification upright: The Hermit upright represents inner search, reflection, solitude, and guidance. Step back to see truth, distill noise into knowing, and seek quiet mentors. Let your inner lamp guide measured steps, and share wisdom when it ripens. True insight comes from reflection and openness.
major_27.name: The Hermit

major_28.signification reversed: The Hierophant reversed warns of dogmatism, outdated rules, or blind obedience. You may be following tradition without understanding its spirit, or resisting necessary change. This card asks you to question edicts that shrink compassion, keep what is wise, and release what is dead. Make tradition alive by practicing its essence, not its shell.
major_28.signification upright: The Hierophant upright represents tradition, teaching, moral guidance, and initiation. Meaning flows through lineage, mentors, and shared rituals. Learn the form to touch the spirit, transmit wisdom with humility, and use good rules to protect freedom and foster belonging. Seek the living principle beneath the custom.
major_28.name: The Hierophant

major_29.signification reversed: The High Priestess reversed can indicate blocked intuition, hidden truths, or superficiality. You may be overriding your inner voice to fit expectations, or staying vague to avoid truth. This card asks you to face secrets kindly, name what you know but haven’t admitted, and simplify inputs to strengthen your signal. Knowledge used to control is a cage; used to understand, it frees.
major_29.signification upright: The High Priestess upright represents intuition, wisdom, mystery, and inner knowledge. Silence becomes a sense organ, and answers surface when you stop pushing and start listening beneath the noise. Dream, journal, notice patterns—what repeats is speaking. Protect your mystery, honor boundaries and timing, and move when inner yes and outer signs align.
major_29.name: The High Priestess

major_30.reversed: wrong choice, separation, indecision, inner conflict
major_30.signification reversed: The Lovers reversed can indicate wrong choice, separation, indecision, or inner conflict. You may be people-pleasing, avoiding loss, or struggling with mixed motives. This card asks you to pause, clear triangulations, and ask what truth you’re avoiding. If parting serves integrity, grieve cleanly and continue—alignment with self is essential.
major_30.signification upright: The Lovers upright represents choice, union, love, duality, and important decision. A values decision may be disguised as romance or options. Choose where desire, honesty, and responsibility coexist. Speak your real yes/no, welcome the same, and let shared direction guide partnership. Depth comes when each remains whole.
major_30.upright: choice, union, love, duality, important decision
major_30.name: The Lovers

major_31.reversed: deception, manipulation, scattered focus, misuse of skills
major_31.signification reversed: The Magician reversed warns of deception, manipulation, scattered focus, or misuse of skills. You may be using charm without integrity, distracting yourself, or trying to control others. This card asks you to reduce inputs, choose one lever, and audit your motives. Re-commit to clean methods, simple systems, and accountable promises—true power is honest and focused.
major_31.signification upright: The Magician upright represents initiative, resources, willpower, energy, and creativity. Attention is your wand—idea, intention, and action align to shape reality. Name the outcome, gather tools, and take one focused step. Communicate clearly, promise realistically, and let momentum compound when will serves a purpose larger than ego.
major_31.name: The Magician

major_32.reversed: clarity, truths revealed, end of illusion
major_32.signification reversed: The Moon reversed signals clarity, truths revealed, or the end of illusion. Fog lifts, facts surface, and your inner sense steadies. This card asks you to proceed with soft confidence and updated maps—trust your intuition and let confusion dissipate.
major_32.signification upright: The Moon upright represents illusion, confusion, fears, subconscious, and mystery. Mist and mirrors abound—move slowly, check projections, and follow somatic cues. Not all threats are real, not all signals are false. Dreamwork and reflection help you navigate uncertainty.
major_32.name: The Moon

major_33.signification reversed: The Star reversed can indicate despair, loss of faith, or pessimism. Hope may be dimmed, but it is not dead. This card asks you to reduce noise, seek small wonders, and let trust regrow through tiny, kept promises. Healing is possible—look for light in unexpected places.
major_33.signification upright: The Star upright represents hope, inspiration, spirituality, and generosity. Light returns after the storm, rehydrating spirit through beauty, kindness, and rest. Share freely, and let grace multiply when given. Trust in renewal and the promise of brighter days.
major_33.name: The Star

major_34.signification reversed: The Sun reversed warns of vanity, inflated ego, or hollow success. You may be polishing without depth, seeking recognition without substance, or losing touch with authenticity. This card asks you to re-root in service and genuine joy—radiance returns when you act from the heart.
major_34.signification upright: The Sun upright represents joy, success, vitality, and celebration. Warmth, visibility, and playful mastery are yours—share credit, savor results, and create from joy. Your light helps others shine, and happiness multiplies when shared.
major_34.name: The Sun

major_35.reversed: resisted change, softened upheaval, gradual restructure
major_35.signification reversed: The Tower reversed can indicate resisted change, softened upheaval, or gradual restructure. You may be avoiding necessary transformation, or trying to control the pace of change. This card asks you to learn now, remove the loose brick, and allow gentle correction before a louder call arrives.
major_35.signification upright: The Tower upright represents shock, revelation, collapse, and liberating change. False structures fall so truth can stand—though abrupt, the clearing is merciful. After the break, rebuild on honest ground with simpler lines. Embrace transformation as a path to freedom.
major_35.name: The Tower

major_36.signification reversed: The World reversed warns of near-miss, perfectionism, or unfinished cycle. You may be struggling to define 'done,' tie the final thread, or let closure stand. This card asks you to complete what needs finishing, accept imperfection, and give yourself the gift of closure for future growth.
major_36.signification upright: The World upright represents completion, harmony, mastery, and wholeness. Integration is achieved—document, celebrate, and share the pattern you’ve mastered. A doorway opens to the next cycle, and fulfillment is found in embracing your journey.
major_36.name: The World

major_37.image_reversed: tarot_img/MajorArcanaCards/La Roue de La Fortune a l'envers.jpg
major_37.signification reversed: Wheel of Fortune reversed signals stagnation, resisting change, or repeating patterns. You may be clinging to what you fear, recreating old loops, or missing opportunities for growth. This card asks you to break cycles by changing one consistent behavior, accept the lesson, and invite a new scene into your life.
major_37.signification upright: Wheel of Fortune upright represents cycles, fate, opportunity, and change. The wheel turns—catch the updraft by staying light and responsive. Notice timing, align with what’s moving, and say yes to real openings. What returns offers a new choice this time—embrace change and trust the flow of life.
major_37.name: Wheel of Fortune
